posts.text:
Italy has recorded a remarkable decline in homicides over the past several decades, with its homicide rate now among the lowest in the European Union.

According to research by Eurispes using official Italian statistics, the country recorded 1,916 homicides in 1991, equivalent to 3.4 per 100,000 inhabitants.

By 2024, that figure had fallen to just 327 homicides, representing a decline of approximately 83% in the annual number of killings.

In 2023, Italy recorded a homicide rate of just 0.57 per 100,000 inhabitants, compared with the EU average of 0.91. When adjusted for age differences between populations, Italy ranked third-lowest in the EU.

The decline has been attributed partly to decades of sustained action against organized crime, declining conflicts between mafia organizations which have reduced their reliance on lethal violence.
